metadata.title: FAQ - Sendero Bike Trails
metadata.description: Answers to common questions about our beginner-friendly bike tours in Colombia's Coffee Region. Safety, weather, fitness levels, and more.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Are the tours safe for beginners?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Yes, all our tours are specifically designed with beginners in mind. We use well-maintained bikes, provide high-quality safety equipment, and our routes avoid heavy traffic. Our experienced guides are trained in first aid and carry safety equipment at all times.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What safety equipment is provided?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] We provide helmets for all riders, reflective vests for better visibility, and our guides carry comprehensive first aid kits. All equipment meets international safety standards.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Are your guides trained in first aid?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Yes, all our guides are certified in wilderness first aid and CPR. They know the locations of the nearest medical facilities along all routes.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What if I have a medical condition?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Please inform us of any medical conditions when booking. Our tours are suitable for people with moderate health, but we recommend consulting your doctor before participating. We can often accommodate specific needs with advance notice.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What's the weather like in Pereira?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Pereira has a mild tropical climate with temperatures ranging from 18-28°C (64-82°F) year-round. The Coffee Region enjoys pleasant weather thanks to its altitude.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] When is the best time to visit?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] The region is beautiful year-round, but the dry seasons (December-March and July-August) offer the most consistent weather for cycling.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What happens if it rains during the tour?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Light rain is common in the Coffee Region and actually adds to the experience. We provide rain gear and adjust routes if needed. Tours are only cancelled in severe weather conditions.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] How fit do I need to be?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Our beginner tours require basic fitness - if you can walk for 2-3 hours comfortably, you can do our tours. E-bikes make cycling accessible even if you're not an experienced cyclist.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What's the difference between beginner and moderate difficulty?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Beginner tours have flat to gentle terrain with frequent breaks, covering 15-25km. Moderate tours include some hills and cover 25-40km with good fitness recommended.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Can I use an e-bike if I'm not confident?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Absolutely! E-bikes are available on all our tours and are perfect for those who want to enjoy the scenery without worrying about fitness level or hills.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What are the average distances per day?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Day tours: 15-30km, Weekend tours: 20-40km per day, Week-long tours: 25-50km per day with rest days included.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] How do I get to Pereira?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Pereira has an international airport (Matecaña Airport - PEI) with connections through Bogotá or Medellín. The airport is 15 minutes from the city center.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Do you offer airport pickup?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Yes, we can arrange airport transfers for an additional fee. Contact us when booking to arrange pickup details.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Is transportation included between tour locations?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] All transportation during the tour is included - we provide support vehicles and transfers between cycling segments.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What equipment is provided?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] We provide: bikes (standard or e-bike), helmets, water bottles, repair kits, and support vehicle. You just bring yourself and appropriate clothing.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What should I pack for the tour?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Comfortable athletic clothing, cycling shorts (padded recommended), sunscreen, sunglasses, light rain jacket, comfortable shoes, and a small daypack. Detailed packing list sent upon booking.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Do I need special cycling shoes?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] No, comfortable athletic or hiking shoes work perfectly. Our bikes have platform pedals suitable for regular shoes.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What about bike sizes?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] We have bikes in all sizes from small to extra-large. We'll ask for your height when booking to ensure the right fit.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Do I need travel insurance?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Yes, we strongly recommend travel insurance that covers cycling activities, medical emergencies, and trip cancellation.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What should my insurance cover?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Your insurance should cover: medical expenses, emergency evacuation, cycling activities, trip cancellation, and personal belongings.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Do I need a visa to visit Colombia?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Many nationalities can visit Colombia visa-free for up to 90 days. Check with your local Colombian embassy for specific requirements based on your nationality.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] How do I book a tour?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Join our waitlist using the form on our homepage. We'll contact you when tours are available with booking instructions and payment details.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What payment methods do you accept?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] We accept credit cards, bank transfers, and PayPal. Full payment details will be provided when tours launch.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What's your cancellation policy?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Cancellation policy details will be provided when tours launch. We aim to offer flexible cancellation terms with full or partial refunds depending on notice period.

questions.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Can I change my tour dates?
questions.answer: [TODO: Update this content] Yes, we understand plans change. Date changes are possible subject to availability and our cancellation policy terms.

aboutPage.title: About Sendero Bike Trails
aboutPage.description: Learn about our mission to provide sustainable, beginner-friendly bike tours in Colombia's Coffee Region.
aboutPage.heading: [PLACEHOLDER] About Us
aboutPage.subtitle: [TODO: Add content] Discover the story behind Sendero and our commitment to sustainable tourism in Colombia's beautiful Coffee Region.

philosophy.heading: [PLACEHOLDER] Brand Philosophy & Story
philosophy.content: [TODO: Add content] We believe that adventure should be accessible to everyone, regardless of fitness level or cycling experience. Sendero was born from a passion for Colombia's stunning Coffee Region and a desire to share its beauty with the world in a sustainable, responsible way. Our journey began with a simple idea: make bike touring beginner-friendly, eco-conscious, and deeply connected to local communities.
philosophy.imageAlt: Sendero team on mountain trail overlooking coffee plantations

region.heading: [PLACEHOLDER] Why the Andes & Coffee Region
region.content: [TODO: Add content] The Coffee Region (Eje Cafetero) is one of Colombia's hidden gems. Nestled in the Andes mountains, Pereira and its surroundings offer breathtaking landscapes, perfect cycling weather year-round, and rich cultural heritage. The rolling hills covered in coffee plantations, cloud forests, and traditional fincas create an ideal backdrop for unforgettable bike adventures. This UNESCO World Heritage region combines natural beauty with authentic local experiences.
region.imageAlt: Scenic coffee plantations in the Andes mountains near Pereira

partners.heading: [PLACEHOLDER] How We Work with Local Fincas
partners.content: [TODO: Add content] Our partnerships with local coffee farms (fincas) are at the heart of what we do. We collaborate directly with family-owned farms to create authentic experiences that benefit local communities. When you tour with Sendero, you're not just visiting - you're supporting sustainable agriculture, fair trade practices, and the preservation of traditional coffee culture. Our finca partners welcome you into their homes, share their stories, and give you hands-on experiences you won't find anywhere else.
partners.imageAlt: Local coffee farm family welcoming visitors to their finca

cta.heading: [PLACEHOLDER] Ready to Explore?
cta.content: [TODO: Add content] Join us for an unforgettable adventure through Colombia's Coffee Region. From beginner-friendly day trips to immersive week-long experiences, we have tours designed for every traveler.

senderoDelTigre.name: El Sendero del Tigre
senderoDelTigre.subtitle: A guided journey through bamboo forests and mountain streams

story.paragraph1: Follow the footsteps of the elusive tigre, through tall grasses, bamboo groves, and the scent of mountain forests.
story.paragraph2: A calm, immersive ride designed to reconnect you with nature, perfect for riders of all levels seeking an authentic Colombian adventure.

stream.title: El Tigre Stream Crossing
stream.description: Wade through crystal-clear mountain waters where wildlife comes to drink. This peaceful stream crossing is a highlight of the trail, offering a refreshing pause in your journey.

bamboo.title: Bamboo Forest Trail
bamboo.description: Ride through towering bamboo groves with dappled sunlight filtering through the canopy. The gentle rustling of bamboo creates a serene atmosphere perfect for nature lovers.

farm.title: Ecological Farm Lunch
farm.description: Traditional Colombian lunch at a sustainable family farm. Enjoy fresh, organic ingredients and learn about local farming practices while surrounded by coffee plants.

vista.title: Mountain Vista Point
vista.description: Panoramic views of coffee plantations and distant peaks. This scenic overlook provides the perfect photo opportunity and a chance to appreciate the Coffee Region landscape.

elevation.heading: Elevation Profile
elevation.description: Mostly gentle rolling terrain with one gradual climb around the midpoint. The elevation changes are manageable for beginners, with no steep descents or technical sections.

testimonial1.quote: One of the most peaceful rides of my life. I felt guided, safe, and deeply connected to the forest. The bamboo section was absolutely magical.

testimonial2.quote: The perfect introduction to cycling in Colombia. Beautiful scenery, authentic experiences, and our guide was incredibly knowledgeable about the local ecology.

testimonial3.quote: The bamboo forests were magical. Our guide knew every plant and bird along the way. Lunch at the farm was a highlight – fresh ingredients and warm hospitality.

datenschutz.purposeText1: We use your data exclusively to send you information and updates about our Bike Tours and to contact you in connection with your interest in our services.
datenschutz.purposeText2: Processing is only carried out on the basis of your consent pursuant to Art. 6 Para. 1 lit. a GDPR.

datenschutz.rightsText1: You have the right at any time to access your stored data, to correct inaccurate data, to delete your data, to restrict processing and to withdraw your consent.

notice.title: Notice: Provisional version

scope.title: Scope
paragraphs: To the extent validly agreed, these terms form part of the package travel contract between the customer (hereinafter the “Traveler”) and Sendero Bike Trails, owner Julian David Perez Rodriguez (hereinafter “Sendero”). They supplement and specify the statutory provisions of §§ 651a–y of the German Civil Code (BGB) and Art. 250 and 252 of the Introductory Act to the German Civil Code (EGBGB).

They apply to all group trips advertised by Sendero and to trips offered individually to private groups. Any deviating arrangements for private groups are stated expressly in the respective offer and in the trip confirmation.
Sendero trips do not include flights to or from Colombia. The Traveler arranges their own travel to and from Colombia; it is not part of the package travel contract.
Before booking, the Traveler receives the standard information form for package travel required by law (Art. 250 § 2 EGBGB) and the pre-contractual information under Art. 250 § 3 EGBGB.

sections.title: 1. Conclusion of the package travel contract

clauses.text: The offer is based on the trip description on senderobiketrails.com, in Sendero presentations or brochures, or on an individual offer, in each case together with any supplementary information available to the Traveler at the time of booking.

By booking (registering for a trip) via the booking form, by email or otherwise in text form, the Traveler makes Sendero a binding offer to conclude the package travel contract. Anyone who books for additional participants is liable for their contractual obligations as for their own, provided they have expressly and separately assumed this obligation.
The contract is concluded when the Traveler receives Sendero’s trip confirmation. The trip confirmation is sent on a durable medium (e.g., as a PDF by email).

If the trip confirmation differs from the booking, it constitutes a new offer by which Sendero is bound for ten days. The contract is concluded on the basis of this new offer if Sendero has pointed out the change and the Traveler accepts it within that period, either expressly or by paying the deposit.
Participants must be at least 18 years old. Minors may take part only by separate agreement and when accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.
There is no statutory right of withdrawal for package trips booked remotely (by phone, email or website) (§ 312(7) BGB). The statutory right to cancel under Section 5 remains unaffected.
Payments toward the trip price before the end of the trip are requested or accepted only upon handing over the insolvency protection certificate (Sicherungsschein, § 651r BGB) in text form.
Once the contract is concluded and the insolvency protection certificate has been received, a deposit of 20% of the trip price is due within 7 days.

The balance is due 30 days before departure. If the trip is still subject to the minimum number of participants (Section 8.1), the balance only becomes due once Sendero can no longer cancel the trip for this reason or has confirmed that it will go ahead.
For bookings made within 30 days of departure, the full trip price is due immediately upon receipt of the insolvency protection certificate.
Payments are made by bank transfer to the account stated on the invoice or via a payment link provided by Sendero. The Traveler bears any bank fees for international transfers.

If the Traveler fails to pay the deposit or balance on time despite having received the insolvency protection certificate, Sendero may, after a reminder setting a deadline, withdraw from the contract and claim compensation in accordance with Section 5.3, unless there is a travel defect that would entitle the Traveler to withdraw.
Without full payment, there is no entitlement to travel documents or travel services.

The scope of services is set out in the trip confirmation together with the trip description valid at the time of booking and the pre-contractual information. Details of stages, distances, elevation gain and trail character are approximate.
Local service providers (e.g., accommodations, transport companies, local guides) are not authorized to make any promises that deviate from the confirmed contract.

Changes to individual travel services after the contract is concluded that Sendero has not brought about in bad faith are permitted, provided they are insignificant and do not affect the overall character of the trip. These include in particular adjustments to the route, daily stages or the order of the program due to weather, trail and road conditions, the security situation or the fitness of the group, replacing an accommodation with an equivalent one, and assigning a different qualified guide. Sendero informs the Traveler of any such changes clearly and comprehensibly on a durable medium before departure.

In the event of a significant change to an essential travel service, the Traveler may, within a reasonable period set by Sendero, accept the change, withdraw from the contract free of charge, or choose an alternative trip if one is offered. If the Traveler does not respond in time, the change is deemed accepted. The notification will point this out.
Warranty claims remain unaffected. If the changed trip or alternative trip is not of equivalent value, the trip price is reduced in accordance with § 651m BGB.

Sendero reserves the right to increase the trip price after the contract is concluded to the extent that this results directly from: (a) an increase in fuel costs for local transport, (b) an increase in taxes and fees (e.g., tourism, park or entrance fees), or (c) a change in the exchange rate between the euro and the Colombian peso (COP), insofar as services are purchased in COP.

The increase corresponds to each Traveler’s share of the additional costs. Sendero notifies the Traveler of it on a durable medium, with reasons and a calculation, no later than 20 days before departure.
The Traveler may request a reduction of the trip price if the costs listed in 4.1 decrease after the contract is concluded and this results in lower costs for Sendero.

If the price increases by more than 8%, the Traveler may, within a reasonable period set by Sendero, withdraw from the contract free of charge or choose an alternative trip. If the Traveler does not respond in time, the increase is deemed accepted.

sections.title: 5. Cancellation by the Traveler before departure, substitute traveler

clauses.text: The Traveler may withdraw from the contract at any time before departure. The cancellation must be declared to Sendero using the contact details below, preferably in text form (email). The date it is received by Sendero is decisive.

If the Traveler cancels or does not start the trip, Sendero loses its claim to the trip price and may instead claim reasonable compensation. This does not apply if Sendero is responsible for the cancellation, or if unavoidable and extraordinary circumstances occur at or near the destination that significantly affect the performance of the trip (e.g., a travel warning issued by the German Federal Foreign Office for the region, natural disasters, serious unrest).

Taking into account saved expenses and the usual possibility of using the travel services otherwise, the compensation is set at the following flat rates (per person, as a percentage of the trip price):

table.label: on the day of departure, or no-show

clauses.text: The Traveler remains free to prove that Sendero has incurred no loss or a significantly lower loss. Instead of the flat rate, Sendero may claim higher compensation calculated on an individual basis if it can prove significantly higher expenses; in that case it must quantify and justify the amount specifically.
If Sendero has to refund payments as a result of the cancellation, the refund is made without undue delay and no later than 14 days after the cancellation.
Taking out trip cancellation and trip interruption insurance is strongly recommended (see Section 12).

Up to 7 days before departure, the Traveler may declare on a durable medium that a substitute will take part in their place (§ 651e BGB). Sendero may object if the substitute does not meet the participation requirements under Section 9. The Traveler and the substitute are jointly and severally liable for the trip price and any additional costs actually incurred; Sendero will provide evidence of these.

There is no entitlement to change the travel date, itinerary, accommodation or scope of services after the contract is concluded (rebooking). This does not apply to rebookings that become necessary because the pre-contractual information was incomplete or incorrect; these are free of charge.

If, at the Traveler’s request, Sendero nevertheless rebooks the trip to a different date up to the 60th day before departure, a rebooking fee of €75 per person is charged, plus any additional costs from service providers. From the 59th day before departure onward, rebooking is only possible by cancelling under the terms of Section 5.3 and making a new booking.

If the Traveler does not use individual services that were duly offered, for reasons for which the Traveler is responsible (e.g., early departure, skipping stages, exclusion under Section 9.5), there is no entitlement to a partial refund. Sendero will try to obtain a refund of saved expenses from the service providers, except for entirely insignificant services.

Sendero may withdraw from the contract if the minimum number of participants stated in the trip description and the trip confirmation is not reached. Unless stated otherwise there, the minimum is 4 Travelers. The cancellation must be declared no later than 30 days before departure. If it becomes clear earlier that the number will not be reached, Sendero will inform the Traveler without undue delay. Payments made are refunded within 14 days. Alternatively, Sendero may offer to run the trip at an adjusted price or offer an alternative trip; the Traveler is not obliged to accept.

If Sendero is prevented from performing the trip by such circumstances (e.g., a travel warning, serious security incidents, natural events, failure of the region’s infrastructure), Sendero may withdraw before departure. The cancellation is declared without undue delay once Sendero becomes aware of the circumstances; payments are refunded within 14 days.

Sendero may terminate the contract without notice if, despite a warning, the Traveler persistently disrupts the trip, repeatedly or grossly disregards the tour leader’s safety instructions, or otherwise acts in breach of contract to such an extent that immediate termination is justified. In that case, Sendero retains its claim to the trip price, less saved expenses and any benefits obtained. The Traveler bears any additional costs of the return journey.

sections.title: 9. Special conditions for guided mountain bike tours

clauses.text: Each trip description sets out the riding skills, fitness, daily distances, elevation gain and altitude (in places above 2,500 m) involved. Before booking, the Traveler checks on their own responsibility whether they meet these requirements and, if in doubt, consults Sendero.

By booking, the Traveler confirms that they are fit enough for the trip booked. Before departure, they complete a participant questionnaire covering riding ability, relevant pre-existing conditions, allergies, medication and an emergency contact. A medical check-up before the trip is recommended for anyone with pre-existing conditions or after a longer break from training. If the Traveler’s health changes significantly after booking, they inform Sendero without undue delay.

Helmets are mandatory on all rides. Gloves and suitable footwear are mandatory; protective gear is recommended or, where stated in the trip description, required. Without a helmet, the Traveler cannot take part in the stage concerned.

Guides working for Sendero and its local partners are entitled, for safety reasons, to change routes, shorten sections, bypass trails, call breaks or have riders push their bikes on certain passages. Their instructions on riding style, spacing within the group and behavior in road traffic must be followed. Colombian traffic rules apply on public roads.

If, in the tour leader’s judgment, a Traveler is visibly overstretched, ill, injured, under the influence of alcohol or without the required equipment, they may be excluded from individual stages for their own safety and that of the group. In such cases, Sendero will, where possible, offer a ride in the support vehicle to the day’s destination. Refunds are only made in accordance with Section 7.

Off-road mountain biking involves risks typical of the sport (e.g., falls, changing surfaces, weather, animals, oncoming traffic on trails). The Traveler rides within their own ability and chooses their own speed and line. This provision does not limit Sendero’s liability for its own breaches of duty, in particular its duties of organization and supervision.

Unless stated otherwise in the trip description, the trip price includes a full-suspension mountain bike in a frame size agreed with the Traveler, including maintenance during the trip. The bike is handed over at the start of the trip in good working order, with a short handover record. By arrangement, the Traveler may bring their own pedals and saddle.

The Traveler treats the rental bike with care, reports any damage or defects to the guide without undue delay, and secures the bike during breaks as the guide instructs. Sendero bears normal wear and tear.

clauses.lead: Liability for damage to the rental bike
clauses.text: For damage or loss beyond normal wear and tear, the Traveler is liable for the full repair costs or current value in cases of intent or gross negligence. In cases of slight negligence, liability is limited to €300 per incident. Damage caused by falls typical of the sport during proper use is not considered negligent.

Instead of the rental bike, the Traveler may bring their own mountain bike. This must be stated when booking or no later than 30 days before departure. The trip price is only reduced if a reduction is stated in the trip description. The bike must be suitable for the advertised trails and in good working order; the tour leader may refuse a bike that is not roadworthy or safe to ride and, where available, provide a rental bike.

Transport, packing and insurance of the Traveler’s own bike on the way to and from Colombia, as well as damage, loss or theft during the trip, are the Traveler’s responsibility, unless Sendero is responsible for a breach of duty. Minor repairs by the support team are carried out without warranty; spare parts are charged at cost. Bike or baggage insurance is recommended.

Once payment has been made in full, the travel documents (meeting point, schedule, emergency contacts) are usually sent by email 14 days before departure. If the Traveler does not receive them in time, they inform Sendero.

The Traveler is responsible for arriving on time at the meeting point or airport transfer stated in the trip confirmation (e.g., Pereira). Sendero recommends booking flights only once the trip has been confirmed (Section 8.1) or on a flexible fare. If the Traveler arrives late, they bear the additional costs of a separate transfer; Sendero is not liable for the cost of flights the Traveler has booked.

The Traveler must report any travel defect without undue delay to the tour leader on site or, if the tour leader cannot be reached, directly to Sendero, and request a remedy. If the Traveler culpably fails to do so and Sendero was therefore unable to remedy the defect, the Traveler has no claim to a price reduction (§ 651m BGB) or damages (§ 651n BGB) in that respect. The tour leader is not authorized to acknowledge claims.

If the Traveler wishes to terminate the contract because of a significant defect (§ 651l BGB), they must first give Sendero a reasonable period to remedy it, unless a remedy is impossible, is refused, or is needed immediately.

Damage to or loss of baggage and bikes during air travel must be reported to the airline on the spot without undue delay using a Property Irregularity Report (P.I.R.) – within 7 days for damage and within 21 days for delay.
The trip price does not include any insurance for the Traveler.

Every Traveler must take out international travel health insurance that covers medical treatment in Colombia, search and rescue, and medically appropriate repatriation to Germany, and that does not exclude cycling/mountain biking. Proof (name of insurer, policy number, emergency number) must be submitted with the participant questionnaire no later than 14 days before departure. Without proof, Sendero may refuse participation in the stages; Section 7 applies accordingly.
Sendero strongly recommends trip cancellation and trip interruption insurance, personal accident and liability insurance that covers cycling abroad, and baggage or bike insurance.
Sendero holds tour operator liability insurance for its activities as a tour operator.

Sendero’s contractual liability for damage that is not bodily injury and was not caused culpably is limited to three times the trip price (§ 651p(1) BGB). Where international conventions or provisions based on them limit or exclude the liability of a service provider for a travel service, Sendero may also rely on them (§ 651p(2) BGB).

Sendero is not liable for performance failures, personal injury or property damage in connection with services that are merely arranged as third-party services (e.g., excursions booked locally, coffee tours, hot springs, paragliding), provided these are expressly identified as third-party services, naming the contracting party, in the trip description and trip confirmation. This does not apply where a breach of Sendero’s duties to inform, advise or organize was the cause.
Sendero is not liable for activities the Traveler undertakes independently outside the program during the trip (e.g., rides in their free time, exploring on their own).
Liability for damage resulting from injury to life, body or health, and for damage caused intentionally or through gross negligence, remains unlimited.

Before the contract is concluded, Sendero provides information on the general passport and visa requirements for Colombia and on health formalities, and on any changes to them before departure. This information applies to citizens of the EU, Switzerland and Liechtenstein without special circumstances (e.g., dual citizenship, statelessness).

The Traveler is responsible for obtaining and carrying their travel documents (a passport with sufficient validity and, where applicable, the Check-MIG online entry form), for any recommended or required vaccinations, and for complying with customs and currency regulations. Any disadvantages resulting from failure to do so are borne by the Traveler, unless Sendero culpably failed to inform them, or informed them inadequately or incorrectly.

The German Federal Foreign Office publishes current travel, safety and medical advice (auswaertiges-amt.de). Sendero recommends seeing a travel medicine specialist before the trip, including about altitude.

On some trips, a photographer commissioned by Sendero accompanies the group at selected points along the route. Images in which the Traveler can be recognized are used for the website, social media or print only with the Traveler’s separate consent, which is requested with the participant questionnaire and can be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future. Consent is not a condition of participation.
Travelers receive the photos of their trip for private, non-commercial use. Copyright remains with the photographer or with Sendero.

Sendero processes the Traveler’s personal data to perform the contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and passes it on only to the service providers in Colombia needed for the trip (e.g., accommodations, the local partner for guiding and transport). Health information from the participant questionnaire is processed only with express consent (Art. 9(2)(a) GDPR), solely for the safe running of the trip and for emergencies, and is deleted no later than 3 months after the end of the trip. Details can be found in the privacy policy on senderobiketrails.com.

Claims under § 651i(3) BGB must be asserted against Sendero using the contact details below, preferably in text form. Under § 651j BGB, claims become time-barred two years after the contractually agreed end of the trip.
Claims may not be assigned to third parties who are not participants in the trip.
Sendero does not take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board and is not obliged to do so (§ 36 VSBG).
The contractual relationship is governed exclusively by German law, even where the travel services are provided in Colombia.

The Traveler may only sue Sendero at its registered place of business (Berlin). For claims brought by Sendero against the Traveler, the Traveler’s place of residence is decisive. For claims against merchants, legal entities and Travelers who have no residence or habitual abode in Germany, or whose residence is unknown, Berlin is agreed as the place of jurisdiction.

These provisions do not apply insofar as mandatory provisions of international agreements, or of the EU member state of which the Traveler is a national, are more favorable to the Traveler. For Travelers resident in Switzerland, the mandatory consumer protection provisions of their country of residence apply.
If individual provisions are invalid, this does not affect the validity of the rest of the travel contract.
